clue.text: Force acquiring thousands by way of business

indicators.note: the word for force takes in, or acquires, a letter in its middle

parts.note: to force someone is to coerce them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them for the plural

explanation.surface: Using pressure to win thousands, a shady way of doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Inevitably, it crumbles

parts.note: alludes to the saying about fate, that's the way the biscuit crumbles

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'that's the way the cookie crumbles' means things turn out as they must.
explanation.definitionFit: A biscuit that, in the saying, always crumbles as fate decrees.

clue.text: Food that makes us extremely slim. lithe and invigorated, for starters

indicators.note: the opening letter of each word is used, like the starter of a meal

explanation.surface: A cereal advert promising to make us slim, lithe and energised.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast food of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Off the cuff, so to speak

definitions.text: Off the cuff, so to speak

parts.words: Off the cuff, so to speak
parts.note: unprepared, as said in impromptu speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'So to speak' signals a figure of speech but also hints at speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken without preparation, impromptu.

clue.text: Such land is an accepted basis of discussion

definitions.text: Such land is an accepted basis of discussion

parts.words: Such land is an accepted basis of discussion
parts.note: shared public land, and figuratively shared points of agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Land shared by all villagers, figuratively the agreed starting point of a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means shared views both parties accept, as well as shared village land.

clue.text: Sculpted statue — that's clever!

indicators.note: sculpting reshapes material, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: An admirer praises a sculptor's statue as clever work.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute is a synonym of shrewd or clever.

clue.text: Plate of fish

definitions.meaning: a thin flake or plate, as of metal or bone
the small overlapping plates that cover a fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate of fish' looks like a dish served up; it is a fish's covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale is a small thin plate forming a fish's protective skin.

clue.text: Employed the Italian in various duties

indicators.note: the Italian article is placed within the shuffled letters
the letters are taken in various orders, rearranged

parts.note: IL is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian worker is given a range of tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Italian' reads as a person in the surface but is just the Italian word for 'the'; 'various' scrambles the duties, giving UTISED, and 'in' sets that word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilised is a synonym of used or employed.

clue.text: Urge school principals to become intellectuals

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
heads run schools

explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is an informal word for highbrow, bookish people.

clue.text: Remove it, as ordered, for extra pay

indicators.note: the letters of the two preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike something off, with extra pay as the reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is the additional wage paid for hours worked beyond the usual.

clue.text: Shaving, father receives phone call

indicators.note: the word for father is followed by, so takes on, the call

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father
to give someone a ring is to phone them

explanation.surface: A man interrupted mid-shave as Dad takes a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A paring is a thin slice shaved off, as from fruit or a fingernail.

clue.text: A singing bank teller?

parts.note: a cashier behind the counter who also sings in a high male voice

explanation.walkthrough: A bank teller works behind a counter; a high male singer has that title.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is the highest adult male singing voice, above tenor.

clue.text: The Muhammedan world is hit

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash someone

explanation.surface: A headline-style claim that the Muslim world has been struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam names the faith and also the whole community of Muslim peoples.

clue.text: Reserved, but singularly partisan

definitions.meaning: something reserved has been put aside, kept apart
taking one party's part only, favouring a single faction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' plays on 'one': a partisan supports one faction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means set aside for later, and also biased towards a single camp.

clue.text: Smith's work with a principal is progressing well

parts.note: a blacksmith shapes metal at the forge, which is forging
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's craft paired with a headteacher, both thriving.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge ahead is to make steady, vigorous progress.

clue.text: Peace for the time being — it's a crime, if one breaks it

indicators.note: breaking the phrase lets its letters be rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A truce is fragile: violating it would be a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges the letters of IT'S A CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, a temporary halt to fighting.

clue.text: Sort of step many debtors neglect to make

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of the following two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of step that many people in debt fail to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges STEP MANY; the surface suggests a step towards solvency.
explanation.definitionFit: Instalments handing over money owed are what defaulting borrowers fail to make.

clue.text: An over-indulgent draughtsman?

parts.note: one who takes too many draughts, swigs of drink, rather than a technical drawer

explanation.walkthrough: A draughtsman draws plans; here it is a man who downs draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard is a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Conclude negotiations about the academic year?

definitions.meaning: to settle a deal by accepting its conditions
a whimsical second reading: being in accord over the three parts of a school or university year

explanation.walkthrough: British schools and universities divide the year into three terms, so the second reading is people agreeing about those terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting conditions ends a bargaining session; the pun reads terms as school periods.

clue.text: Yet you may feel so, if taken in by somebody

definitions.text: Yet you may feel so, if taken in by somebody

parts.words: Yet you may feel so, if taken in by somebody
parts.note: being sheltered as a guest seems the opposite of being turned away, yet a deceived person feels annoyed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' means given shelter or deceived; the deceived feel annoyed, though being sheltered is the opposite of being turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means annoyed or inconvenienced, which a deceived person feels.

clue.text: A story, for example, viewed in advance

indicators.note: the abbreviation is seen inside the word for advance

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A tale, such as one previewed beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story or myth.

clue.text: Food from the earth — £500 to an aficionado

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
a nut is a keen fan, as in a golf nut

explanation.surface: A fan handed £500 for some produce dug from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is British betting slang for £500.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey nut, or peanut, ripens underground, so it is literally food from the earth.

clue.text: We hear forty of the Romans distinguish themselves

indicators.note: signals that the letters are said out loud to give a word

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Talk of forty Romans who win distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear': XL said aloud is ex-ell.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to stand out, to outdo others.

clue.text: Impertinence one might get from a waiter

definitions.text: one might get from a waiter
definitions.meaning: a condiment such as gravy or ketchup brought to the table

explanation.walkthrough: The waiter could hand over cheek as readily as a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cheek in British slang and also a liquid relish served with food.

clue.text: Shade that makes little difference

definitions.meaning: a subtle variation, as in a shade of meaning
a slight distinction, one that differs by only a little

explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine gradation of meaning or colour, a tiny difference.

clue.text: Poison counter

parts.note: reads like someone tallying toxins, but means a remedy that counters a toxin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a noun, one who counts; here it is what works against.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that neutralises a toxin.

clue.text: Bottom place on top of a mount

definitions.text: Bottom place on top of a mount

parts.words: Bottom place on top of a mount
parts.note: the seat where a rider's backside sits on a horse's back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a mountain, but it is a horse, and 'Bottom' is the rider's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the rider's seat strapped onto a horse's back.

clue.text: Stopped and taken into custody

explanation.definitionFit: The word means halted in progress, and also detained by police.
